A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ALM research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v3 reports original tokenizer-transfer, ensembling, mathematical-reasoning distillation and hypernetwork results, alongside experimental analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds Gemma3 12B tokenizer-transfer results in Table 5.

M1.justification: The ALM objective, outcome debiasing, hidden-state loss, GradMag and byte-transfer/hypernetwork adaptations remain unchanged. Appendix I documents implementation of the existing procedure rather than establishing a method revision.

E1.justification: The training datasets, benchmark tasks, languages and tokenizer-transfer scenarios are retained. The added Gemma3 experiment changes the model configuration within existing subword-transfer coverage, without introducing new data or task requirements.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their comparison methods, including SFT, DSKD, MinED and the appendix comparators. The new Gemma3 comparison reuses SFT; it introduces no new baseline or removal from an existing comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 adds evaluation of Gemma3 12B IT transferred to the Qwen2 tokenizer using the retained benchmark metrics. Previously reported training and evaluation settings, including Appendix B's defaults, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.1 adds a limited scaling analysis comparing transfer-gap reduction for Gemma2 2B and Gemma3 12B. Existing learning-rate, temperature, debiasing, loss-balancing, hypernetwork and ensemble-pivot analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains identical uncertainty reporting. No seed counts, repeated-run information or statistical estimation procedures are added or revised; the new Table 5 reports point estimates.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports Gemma3 12B averages of 71.2 for the original model, 64.6 for SFT and 69.2 for ALM. These are additional-model results, not updates under the earlier model settings. All eleven v3 tables retain identical entries in v4 Tables 1–4 and 6–12.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, temperature-limit derivations, divergence proof and tokenization-bias formalism are retained. Appendix I's matrix expressions provide a computational restatement of existing chunk aggregation and loss mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are unchanged, and the introduction retains the same central contributions and three use cases. Additional scaling evidence supports the existing claims without redefining the paper's core contribution.

C2.justification: v4 adds an expected relationship between vocabulary-size differences and transfer difficulty, and discusses when direct transfer versus hypernetwork training may be more efficient. It revises the model-scale limitation after the 12B experiment and explicitly highlights uncertainty about larger training budgets and optimal chunk selection.

D1.justification: New Appendix I explains single-pass byte-boundary alignment, binary chunk-membership matrices, batched log-probability aggregation and preparation in a separate data-loading thread. Existing hyperparameters, hardware information and code/model access disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to Xu et al. (2024), Fu et al. (2023), Needleman and Wunsch (1970), and the Gemma 3 technical report. Appendix I adds a focused comparison between byte-boundary alignment and prior edit-distance alignment approaches; the broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v4 adds Section 4.1 and Appendix I, expands several explanatory passages and revises limitations. It also updates the conference footer and funding acknowledgment. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figure 2 illustrating outcome chunk debiasing and Table 5 displaying Gemma3 results. Existing figures and tables retain their content and basic design, with renumbering and relocation as the surrounding text reflows.

improvement.justification: The Gemma3 12B experiment partly addresses v3's lack of evidence beyond 8B parameters. The debiasing illustration, implementation appendix and more specific applicability discussion also improve clarity and reproducibility. These are focused gains: the scaling evidence adds only one model, while the earlier results and theory remain unchanged.
